why: This run is not a measurement and should not be read as a point on any curve. It was started against an app server whose JVM was 2 minutes 49 seconds old, and its own metadata asserts a cache policy that was false. The record is corrected additively; run-metadata.json is left exactly as the run wrote it, because editing a completed run's own record to say something it did not say would falsify it.

notMeasurement.reason: started 2 minutes 49 seconds after the app server's JVM, which costs roughly two thirds of throughput

basis: the app server's JVM (pid 1167) started 2026-10-05T11:34:14Z, read from `ps -eo lstart` on the host; the instance itself booted at 11:30:56Z
app server CPU held 99.19-99.22% across both runs at 1-minute resolution, the same ceiling the warm runs reach -- so the server was not doing less work, it was getting less done per CPU-second
RDS CPU 14-33%, ReadIOPS 0.0 and ReadLatency 0.0 throughout: the database buffer cache had already refilled, so what was cold was not the database
the injector idled at 3-22% CPU across 4 vCPU, load average 0.00
the same two windows re-run at 12:01 and 12:02, on the same JVM twenty minutes older and after two saturating passes, returned 50.00 and 56.58 rps against 18.43 and 30.94
it failed 0.21% of its requests against its own recorded MAX_FAILED_PERCENT gate of 0.05%, and Gatling asserted and failed at the time
only 91 of its 100 devices completed a sync; 108 of 4,300 requests were never issued because a failed request ends that user's chain
cause: The environment had been stopped and started, and the runs were issued once /ping answered 200 rather than once the server had had traffic through it. CACHE_POLICY was passed explicitly as `warm-incidental-no-reset` -- build.gradle defaults the field to `unrecorded`, so this was an assertion rather than a default, and nothing in the run could contradict it.
fixedBy: avni-perf prepare-run.sh step 6 -- every measured run is a warm run, and the warm-up pass is discarded
avni-infra provision/scripts/env-warmup.sh -- env-teardown.sh start warms the server automatically and throws the result away
keptBecause: These two runs are the evidence for the cold-start finding in docs/findings-case1.md, which matters in production because every avni-server deploy restarts the JVM. They are excluded from the curve, not discarded.
